subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- August 29, 2026
body:
Subject: geocode-glib update conflict fixed in AcreetionOS

The geocode-glib update conflict that bit installed AcreetionOS systems is resolved. A repair branch landed today with the fix merged into the main repos, so anyone who hit the file conflict during pacman -Syu should be able to refresh cleanly now without manual intervention.

Development

Darren pushed two related commits to the calamares-config repo worth flagging. Older NVIDIA cards now get a working installer path again, and disk encryption has been pulled out of the default flow — users can still opt in later if they want full-disk crypto, but the default install is simpler and boots more reliably on a wider range of hardware. He also tweaked GRUB to prefer 1080p over native 4K during boot, which kills a class of blank-screen reports we kept seeing on high-DPI panels. Full notes are up at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html.

Community

Two pieces of press worth your time. BetaNews ran a feature calling AcreetionOS the easy-to-use alternative to Windows 10 and 11, which is nice validation as the Windows 10 end-of-support wave keeps pushing folks toward Linux. Phoronix also reported that a prominent Arch Linux developer resigned after a ten-year run, a reminder that the ecosystem we build on is held together by people, and people move on. Stay kind to your maintainers.

Tip of the day

If you skipped the last couple of system updates because of the geocode-glib conflict, run sudo pacman -Syu today. The fix is in. If you are on a machine with an older NVIDIA card or a 4K laptop panel and have been holding off on a fresh install, the updated ISO is the one to grab — head to https://acreetionos.org/flash.html and reinstall from scratch for the cleanest experience. Existing installs just need the update plus a reboot. Docs for troubleshooting the Calamares installer live at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html if anything still looks off after upgrading.

— The AcreetionOS crew
